This is why AH and YU must be *separate* force objects with *identical* exclusion sets: exclusions are declared per-force in OpenMM, so every force that models a pair interaction needs the exclusion replayed.

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L500-L528), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L487-L498)

Finally, forces are registered into the `System` (`add_forces_to_system`) and organized into force groups — AH in group 0 and YU in group 1 for non-lipid systems, or groups 1 and 3 respectively within the five-force lipid layout. Force groups are what make per-interaction energy reporting possible downstream.

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L317-L334), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L269-L292)

For restrained pairs — pairs excluded from the global AH/YU forces because a restraint already connects them — the module provides pairwise re-incarnations of both potentials as `CustomBondForce` objects: `init_scaled_LJ` reproduces the AH piecewise form with per-bond parameters `s`, `l`, and a scaling factor `n` (`comp.bondscale[i,j]`), while `init_scaled_YU` reproduces the shifted Yukawa form with a hard-coded 4.0 nm reference distance for the shift. These variants are consumed by Go-type restraint construction and are examined on the restraints page.

Sources: [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L137-L158), [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L189-L196), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L95-L101)

## End-to-End Validation Strategy

`tests/test_potentials.py` validates both potentials *through the full simulation stack*, not in isolation. The reference analytic forms are defined as NumPy lambdas mirroring the expressions above:

```python
HALR = lambda r,s,l : 4*0.8368*l*((s/r)**12-(s/r)**6)              # AH tail
HASR = lambda r,s,l : 4*0.8368*((s/r)**12-(s/r)**6)+0.8368*(1-l)   # AH wall
HA   = lambda r,s,l : np.where(r<2**(1/6)*s, HASR(r,s,l), HALR(r,s,l))
HASP = lambda r,s,l,rc : np.where(r<rc, HA(r,s,l)-HA(rc,s,l), 0)   # cutoff-shifted AH
DHSP = lambda r,yukawa_eps,lD,rc : np.where(r<rc, DH(r,yukawa_eps,lD)-DH(rc,...), 0)
```

The constant 0.8368 kJ/mol is exactly the default `eps_lj` after the kcal→kJ conversion in `Sim.__init__`, confirming the test targets the production code path rather than a parallel implementation.

Sources: [test_potentials.py](tests/test_potentials.py#L11-L19), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L42)

The test harness builds minimal two-particle systems — one bead of each of five residue pairs (e.g. E–R, E–W) in an 8 nm box at 298 K and 0.15 M ionic strength — runs the simulation via `sim.run`, then replays the physics analytically:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Config: 8 nm box, 298 K, 0.15 M,<br/>report_potential_energy = True"] --> B["Two single-residue components<br/>(uncharged termini)"]
    B --> C["sim.run → DCD trajectory + energy log"]
    C --> D["mdtraj: bead–bead distance series"]
    D --> E["HASP: analytic AH, rc = 2 nm"]
    D --> F["DHSP: analytic DH, rc = 4 nm<br/>ε from q1·q2·lB·kT, lD from ionic"]
    E --> G["u_calc = u_ah + u_dh"]
    F --> G
    G --> H{"np.allclose(u, u_calc,<br/>rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-8)"}
```

Note the subtle detail: the test reconstructs `yukawa_eps` per residue pair from the *residues.csv charges* (`q₁·q₂·lB·RT`) rather than calling `genParamsDH` directly, so both the parameterization math and the OpenMM expression are verified independently. Any drift between the shipped energy expressions and the analytic reference — a typo in the shift, a wrong `step` polarity, a mismatched cutoff — breaks the `rtol=1e-3` agreement and fails the build.

Sources: [test_potentials.py](tests/test_potentials.py#L21-L95), [test_potentials.py](tests/test_potentials.py#L97-L126)

## Key Implementation Insights

> [!TIP]
> The AH λ-mixing rule lives *inside* the energy expression, not in Python. Because OpenMM parses `l=select((id1+id2)*step(id1+id2), 0.5*(l1+l2), fixed_lambda)` per pair at runtime, adding a new particle class (e.g. a new crowder variant) requires only a new `id` value in `add_interactions` — no new force object, no Python-level pair loop. This is also why the crowder is "free": it reuses the protein force with id = −1.

> [!TIP]
> `genParamsDH` must run before `make_components` in `build_system` — the code comments this explicitly — because Go-type restraints bind `eps_yu`/`k_yu` into per-bond scaled forces at component-creation time. Reordering these two calls breaks every restrained system with an uninitialized-parameter error.

## Where to Go Next

The potentials documented here are the "plain" non-lipid regime of CALVADOS. Natural continuations within the catalog:

- **[Lipid Interactions: WCA And SA Terms](11-lipid-interactions-wca-and-sa-terms)** — the five-force regime: `init_wca_interactions`, `init_ah_lipid_interactions`, and `init_sa_interactions` with geometric λ/ω mixing.
- **[Force Groups And Interaction Exclusions](12-force-groups-and-interaction-exclusions)** — the exclusion-map mechanics and force-group layout referenced in §5.
- **[AF-Guided Harmonic And Go Restraints](13-af-guided-harmonic-and-go-restraints)** — where `init_scaled_LJ`/`init_scaled_YU` re-introduce AH/YU between restrained pairs.
- **[Sequence Processing And Charge States](6-sequence-processing-and-charge-states)** — how `comp.qs` (the per-particle Yukawa charges) are derived from sequence, pH, and termini settings.
- **[Testing Potentials And Bond Topologies](22-testing-potentials-and-bond-topologies)** — the broader test-suite context surrounding `test_potentials.py`.


# Lipid Interactions: WCA And SA Terms



This page documents the nonbonded force field machinery that MEM-CALVADOS deploys when lipids are present in a system. In lipid-free simulations, all nonbonded physics is carried by two forces (Ashbaugh–Hatch and Debye–Hückel). Once a single lipid bead is registered, `Sim.build_system` switches to a **five-force decomposition** in which the Weeks–Chandler–Andersen (WCA) term and the Solvent-Accessible (SA) term each own a precisely defined slice of the pair space. We cover the exact energy expressions, the mixing rules, the cutoff selection logic, the bead-classification scheme (TMT thresholds), and the interaction-group topology that makes the five forces a disjoint partition of all nonbonded pairs.

Sources: [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L26-L90), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L160-L181)

## Why Lipids Force A Different Architecture

The design decision lives in one branch point: if `self.nlipids > 0`, the builder instantiates five `CustomNonbondedForce` objects — `wca`, `ah_pp`, `ah` (the lipid-tuned Ashbaugh–Hatch variant), `sa`, and `yu`. Otherwise it falls back to the canonical two-force scheme (`ah` + `yu`). The commented-out lines alongside (`wca_pl`, `ah_ll`, `ah_pl`, `yu_ll`, …) reveal the earlier design intent — one force per pair-type combination — which was abandoned in favor of a single force per *energy functional form*, with pair selectivity delegated to OpenMM interaction groups.

This matters for advanced developers because the energy expressions are global: every particle in the system is registered in **all five forces** with its `(sigma, lambda, omega, q)` parameters, and the actual pair coverage is carved out exclusively by `addInteractionGroup` calls. Changing which beads belong to which class therefore reshapes the entire interaction matrix without touching a single energy expression.

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L160-L181), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L500-L528)

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Forces["Five CustomNonbondedForce instances (nlipids > 0)"]
        WCA["wca — force group 0<br/>purely repulsive core"]
        AHPP["ah_pp — force group 1<br/>Ashbaugh-Hatch, protein x protein"]
        AHL["ah — force group 1<br/>Lipid AH: unshifted LJ * l"]
        SA["sa — force group 2<br/>smooth polynomial attraction"]
        YU["yu — force group 3<br/>Debye-Huckel, charged x charged"]
    end
    PROT["protein beads"] --> AHPP
    PROT --> SA
    PROT --> AHL
    SER["lipid_ser (-4 <= tmt < 0)"] --> AHL
    SER --> WCA
    LTL["lipid_ltl tails (tmt > 0)"] --> SA
    LTL --> WCA
    CHD["lipid_chd heads (-5 <= tmt < -4)"] --> WCA
    MID["MID beads (tmt < -5)"] --> WCA
    CHG["all charged beads"] --> YU
```

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L269-L292)

## The WCA Term: Purely Repulsive Excluded Volume

The WCA force is constructed by `init_wca_interactions(eps, rc)` with the energy expression:

```
4*eps*((s/r)^12-(s/r)^6+0.25)*step(rmin-r);  rmin=2^(1/6)*s;  s=0.5*(s1+s2)
```

The `+0.25` constant is the standard WCA **value shift**: at the Lennard-Jones minimum `rmin = 2^(1/6)·s`, the bracket evaluates to `4·(0.25 − 0.5 + 0.25) = 0`, and the analytic derivative of the 12-6 branch also vanishes at `rmin`. The `step(rmin-r)` gate then zeroes everything at larger separations, so WCA contributes neither energy nor force beyond contact. This is why the repulsive core is C¹-continuous — a property the developer relies on implicitly, since the AH-lipid and SA expressions reuse the identical branch for their `r < rmin` regimes.

Note that WCA defines no attractive term at all and mixes only the size parameter (`s = 0.5·(s1+s2)`, arithmetic mean); there is no `lambda` or `omega` per-particle parameter — beads carry only `[sig]` when registered. The force uses `CutoffPeriodic` with `rc = self.cutoff_wca`, which `build_system` computes as `2**(1/6) * max(sigma)` over **all** components — the largest possible contact distance, guaranteeing the cutoff never truncates the (finite) support of the potential.

Sources: [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L26-L38), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L161-L165)

## The SA Term: Smooth, Finite-Range Attraction

`init_sa_interactions(eps, rc)` implements the solvent-accessibility-motivated attractive term:

```
eps*select(step(r-rmin),
    l*(3*u^2-2*u^3-1)*step(rmin+o-r),
    4*((s/r)^12-(s/r)^6+0.25)-l);
u=(r-rmin)/o; rmin=2^(1/6)*s; s=0.5*(s1+s2); l=sqrt(l1*l2); o=sqrt(o1*o2)
```

Three regime behaviors follow directly from the expression. For `r < rmin`, particles feel the familiar WCA core offset by `−l`. For `rmin ≤ r ≤ rmin + o` (with `o > 0`), the attraction is a cubic polynomial in the reduced distance `u`: it starts at exactly `−l` when `u = 0` (since `3·0 − 2·0 − 1 = −1`), rises with zero slope at both ends, and terminates at exactly `0` when `u = 1` (`3 − 2 − 1 = 0`). The inner `step(rmin+o-r)` hard-truncates the term beyond `rmin + o`. The whole function is therefore C¹-continuous at `rmin` (the WCA branch has zero slope there, as does the polynomial at `u = 0`), and reaches zero smoothly at the outer boundary — no force discontinuities anywhere in its support.

The three per-particle parameters are `[sig, lam, ome*nm]`, and mixing uses **geometric means** for both attractiveness and range: `l = √(l1·l2)`, `o = √(o1·o2)`. The `omega` value — the pair-dependent attraction length — is read from the optional `omega` column of the component's residues table, so lipid systems require a residue file that defines it for every bead type. This is a hard requirement, not a convenience: `cutoff_sa = max(2**(1/6)*sig + ome)` is computed only over beads with `ome > 0`, and `add_interactions` unconditionally zips `comp.omegas` for every component in a lipid system.

Sources: [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L75-L90), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L163-L171), [components.py](calvados/components.py#L60-L61), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L508-L513)

> [!TIP]
> Unlike a shifted truncated LJ tail, the SA attraction is anchored at `−l` exactly at contact and decays over a *per-pair* distance `√(o1·o2)`. Two beads with `omega = 0` contribute no SA attraction regardless of `l` — the cutoff scan explicitly skips them (`if ome > 0`). Tune membrane cohesion by editing the `omega` column, not `lambdas`.

## The Lipid AH Variant: Attractive Headgroup Chemistry

For lipid-bearing systems, the force named `ah` is *not* the standard Ashbaugh–Hatch potential of the non-lipid branch — it is `init_ah_lipid_interactions(eps, rc)`:

```
eps*select(step(r-rmin), 4*l*((s/r)^12-(s/r)^6), 4*((s/r)^12-(s/r)^6+0.25)-l);
shift=(s/rc)^12-(s/rc)^6; rmin=2^(1/6)*s; s=0.5*(s1+s2); l=sqrt(l1*l2)
```

For `r ≥ rmin` this is an **unshifted** 12-6 Lennard-Jones scaled by `l` — the `shift` variable is defined but unused, signaling the cutoff energy offset is deliberately not applied, so the full attractive well (depth `−l` at `rmin`) is preserved and decays to the cutoff. For `r < rmin` the branch is the WCA core minus `l`, matching the SA construction exactly.

Comparing the three LJ-family expressions side by side exposes the design grammar:

| Force | `r < rmin` branch | `r ≥ rmin` branch | Attraction range | `l` mixing | Extra params |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `init_ah_interactions` (protein/RNA, also `ah_pp`) | WCA core `+ (1−l)` | shifted LJ · `l` | shifted LJ to `rc` | arithmetic `0.5·(l1+l2)` via `id` select, else `fixed_lambda` | `s`, `l`, `id` |
| `init_ah_lipid_interactions` (`ah`) | WCA core `− l` | **unshifted** LJ · `l` | unshifted LJ to `rc` | geometric `√(l1·l2)` | `s`, `l` |
| `init_sa_interactions` (`sa`) | WCA core `− l` | `l·(3u²−2u³−1)` | exactly `rmin + o` | geometric `√(l1·l2)` | `s`, `l`, `o` |
| `init_wca_interactions` (`wca`) | WCA core only | zero | none | — | `s` |

The full Ashbaugh–Hatch expression resolves `l` through `select((id1+id2)*step(id1+id2), 0.5*(l1+l2), fixed_lambda)`: arithmetic mixing activates only when the sum of the `id` parameters is non-negative. In lipid systems every particle is registered with `id = 1` in `ah_pp` (so arithmetic mixing always applies there), whereas in lipid-free systems crowders receive `id = −1`, steering their mixed pairs toward `fixed_lambda`.

Sources: [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L40-L73), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L508-L525)

## Bead Classification: The TMT Column Drives Everything

During particle registration, `build_system` routes each bead into named index sets by comparing its `tmt` residue-table column against fixed thresholds. The names (defined in [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L212-L218) with comments marking CHO/PHO charged heads and MID beads) map to the thresholds as follows:

| Condition | Index set | Role in the interaction matrix |
|---|---|---|
| `tmt < -5` | `tmt_mid` → `lipid_mid` | MID beads, repulsion-only partners |
| `-5 <= tmt < -4` | `tmt_chd` → `lipid_chd` | charged headgroups (CHO, PHO) |
| `-4 <= tmt < 0` | `tmt_neg` → `lipid_ser` | serine/linker-class beads with attractive chemistry |
| `tmt > 0` | `tmt_pos` → `lipid_ltl` | hydrophobic tails |
| charge ≠ 0 | `charged_indices` | Debye–Hückel participation |

`lipid_indices` and `protein_indices` are accumulated independently of the TMT scan, and the lipid-specific sets are finally intersected with `lipid_indices` so that the same thresholds applied to protein rows cannot leak protein beads into lipid classes.

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L212-L263), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L269-L274)

## Interaction Group Topology: A Disjoint Partition Of Pair Space

The five `addInteractionGroup` calls together cover every chemically admissible pair exactly once. Reading them as (set A × set B):

| Force | Set A | Set B | Pairs covered |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wca` | `lipid_ser` | `lipid_ltl ∪ lipid_mid` | ser–tail, ser–MID (repulsion only) |
| `wca` | `protein ∪ lipid_ltl ∪ lipid_chd ∪ lipid_mid` | `lipid_mid ∪ lipid_chd` | head/MID against proteins, tails, and each other |
| `ah_pp` | `protein` | `protein` | protein–protein Ashbaugh–Hatch |
| `ah` | `lipid_ser` | `lipid_chd ∪ lipid_ser ∪ protein` | serine-attractive contacts (head, ser, protein) |
| `sa` | `protein ∪ lipid_ltl` | `lipid_ltl` | smooth attraction involving tails |
| `yu` | `charged` | `charged` | all Debye–Hückel pairs (overlay, not part of the partition) |

Cross-checking the 15 possible class pairs confirms the partition property: protein–protein → `ah_pp`; ser × {ser, chd, protein} → `ah`; tail pairs and protein–tail → `sa`; everything involving `chd` or `mid` (except ser's attractive slots) → `wca`. No pair receives two non-electrostatic contributions, and none receives zero. The forces are grouped for reporting as: `wca` → group 0, `ah_pp` and `ah` → group 1 (their energies sum in per-group output), `sa` → group 2, `yu` → group 3 — a layout the `ForceGroupReporter` can exploit to attribute virial/energy components per interaction class.

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L275-L292)

> [!TIP]
> Because `ah_pp` and `ah` share force group 1, per-group energy traces do not separate protein–protein from lipid-head attraction. If you need them separated for analysis, reassign one force to a fresh group in `build_system` and update `print_system_summary` accordingly.

## Cutoff Selection And Parameter Flow

Cutoffs are chosen per force at initialization time, before any particle exists. `cutoff_wca` is `2^(1/6) · max(σ)` across all components — conservative, since WCA is identically zero past `rmin`, but cheap and safe. `cutoff_sa` is `max(2^(1/6)·σ + ω)` restricted to beads with `ω > 0` — the minimal radius that fully contains every smooth-tail support. `ah`, `ah_pp`, and `yu` reuse the user-supplied `cutoff_lj` and `cutoff_yu` from the YAML config, and the global `eps_lj` is unit-converted from kcal to kJ/mol in the `Sim` constructor before ever reaching an energy expression.

Per-particle registration (`add_interactions`) then gives **every bead of every component** a slot in all five forces: `[sig]` for `wca`, `[sig, lam, 1]` for `ah_pp`, `[sig, lam]` for `ah`, `[sig, lam, ome·nm]` for `sa`, and `[q]` for `yu`. Since OpenMM evaluates a `CustomNonbondedForce` only for pairs inside its interaction groups, this "register everywhere, compute selectively" pattern keeps parameter bookkeeping uniform while the TMT-driven groups remain the single source of truth for pair physics.

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L41-L42), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L161-L174), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L500-L528)

## Exclusions And Bonded Context For Lipid Chains

The `Lipid` component supplies the bonded scaffolding that WCA/SA are meant to complement: consecutive beads (`j == i+1`) get harmonic bonds with per-bead `bondk`, and every triple (`i`, `i+1`, `i+2`) gets a harmonic angle with per-bead `angle`/`anglek`. Both `add_bonds` and `add_angles` return exclusion maps that `Sim.add_exclusions` applies to **all five nonbonded forces**, so 1-2 and 1-3 neighbors along a lipid chain are invisible to WCA, AH, SA, and Debye–Hückel alike; 1-4 and beyond still interact. The same exclusion pathway is reused by restraints and custom restraints, which automatically silence all nonbonded terms on restrained pairs. At build completion, `print_system_summary` reports particle and exclusion counts per force — the quickest sanity check that your TMT assignments and residue table produced the expected topology.

Sources: [components.py](calvados/components.py#L450-L524), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L456-L498), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L382-L387)

## Seeing It In Practice

The bilayer example instantiates this machinery end-to-end: it computes `N_lipids = ceil(Lx·Ly/area_per_lipid)·2` for a 0.6 nm² area per lipid, sets `topol = 'bilayer'` with `bilayer_eq = True` (the `MonteCarloMembraneBarostat` that pairs naturally with these interaction terms), and registers one component as `molecule_type = 'lipid'` using a local `residues.csv` that must carry the `tmt`, `omega`, `bondk`, `angle`, and `anglek` columns the lipid path expects. Lipid placement uses `place_bilayer` on the `bilayergrid` rather than the protein-oriented topology grids, and molecule counting in `count_components` moves proteins to the front of the component array while tallying `nlipids` — the flag that triggers the entire five-force path described above.

Sources: [examples/bilayer/prepare.py](examples/bilayer/prepare.py#L16-L66), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L107-L137), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L438-L454)

## Where To Go Next

The expressions documented here are the lipid-specific members of the broader potential family: the protein/RNA side — including the full Ashbaugh–Hatch `select` logic and the Debye–Hückel parameter derivation — is covered in [Ashbaugh-Hatch And Yukawa Potentials](10-ashbaugh-hatch-and-yukawa-potentials). The force-group bookkeeping introduced at the end of this page (groups 0–3, per-group reporting, exclusion propagation) is expanded in [Force Groups And Interaction Exclusions](12-force-groups-and-interaction-exclusions). For how lipids get placed into bilayer geometry before these forces act on them, see [Bilayer Assembly And Topologies](9-bilayer-assembly-and-topologies), and for the membrane barostat that equilibrates systems built on WCA/SA cohesion, continue to [Slab Equilibration And Barostats](15-slab-equilibration-and-barostats).

# Force Groups And Interaction Exclusions



In CALVADOS, every simulation is assembled from a collection of independent OpenMM `Force` objects. Two pieces of bookkeeping turn that collection into a well-defined, efficient, and analyzable energy model: **force group assignment** (which forces are summed into which numbered energy bucket) and **interaction exclusions** (which particle pairs are silently skipped by each nonbonded force). This page documents both mechanisms as they are actually implemented in `sim.py`, `interactions.py`, `components.py`, and `forcegroupreporter.py`. It assumes you already know what the Ashbaugh-Hatch, Yukawa, WCA, and SA potentials *are* — the physics lives in [Ashbaugh-Hatch And Yukawa Potentials](10-ashbaugh-hatch-and-yukawa-potentials) and [Lipid Interactions: WCA And SA Terms](11-lipid-interactions-wca-and-sa-terms); here we cover how those forces are partitioned and pruned.

## Architectural Role: Two Orthogonal Pruning Mechanisms

CALVADOS uses three distinct mechanisms to control *which pairs a force evaluates*, and it is worth separating them from first principles because they operate at different levels:

1. **Force groups** (`setForceGroup(n)`) — a pure energy-accounting concept. The force still evaluates every eligible pair; the group number only determines which bucket `Context.getState()` reports its energy into.
2. **Interaction groups** (`addInteractionGroup(setA, setB)`) — a `CustomNonbondedForce`-level filter. Pairs not drawn from `setA × setB` are never evaluated, saving compute.
3. **Exclusions** (`addExclusion(i, j)`) — a pair-level blacklist. Specific (i, j) pairs are removed from the force entirely, typically because their interaction is handled by an explicit bonded term instead.

The following concept diagram shows how a molecule's beads flow through these three mechanisms in `Sim.build_system`:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph M["One molecule's beads (components.py)"]
        B["bond_check pairs"] --> EB["exclusion_map entries"]
        A["angle_check pairs"] --> EB
        R["restrained pairs"] --> EB
    end
    subgraph IG["Interaction groups (sim.py)"]
        TMT["TMT/charge-based index sets"] --> IW["wca: ser ↔ ltl+mid ..."]
        TMT --> IPP["ah_pp: protein × protein"]
        TMT --> IYU["yu: charged × charged"]
    end
    EB -->|"add_exclusions()"| X["addExclusion(i,j) on every nonbonded force"]
    IW & IPP & IYU --> F["setForceGroup(0..3)"]
    X --> F
    F --> RPT["ForceGroupReporter: per-group energy traces"]
```

The exclusion map is generated *inside* each component class (`components.py`), while group assignment and interaction-group pruning happen *centrally* in `Sim.build_system` (`sim.py`) after all molecules are placed. This split — per-component pair bookkeeping, central force orchestration — is the core architectural pattern of the page.

Sources: [sim.py](/calvados/sim.py#L269-L292), [components.py](/calvados/components.py#L94-L105), [forcegroupreporter.py](/calvados/forcegroupreporter.py#L17-L20)

## The Force Group Map: Two Layouts Depending on Lipid Content

`Sim.build_system` assigns explicit force groups only after all molecules have been added (sim.py L269-L292). The layout depends on whether the system contains lipids, because lipid systems split the Ashbaugh-Hatch attraction into multiple force objects:

| System type | Force | Purpose | Force group |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lipid systems | `wca` | WCA repulsion on lipid chains and heads | 0 |
| Lipid systems | `ah_pp` | Ashbaugh-Hatch, protein × protein | 1 |
| Lipid systems | `ah` | Ashbaugh-Hatch, lipid tail ↔ head/protein | 1 |
| Lipid systems | `sa` | Short-range attraction (SA term) | 2 |
| Lipid systems | `yu` | Debye-Hückel / Yukawa electrostatics | 3 |
| Non-lipid | `ah` | Single Ashbaugh-Hatch force for everything | 0 |
| Non-lipid | `yu` | Yukawa electrostatics | 1 |

A critical subtlety: **group 0 is the OpenMM default**. Every force that never calls `setForceGroup` — the `HarmonicBondForce` (`hb`), `HarmonicAngleForce` (`ha`), harmonic/Go restraints (`cs`), custom restraints (`cres`), scaled LJ/YU bond terms (`scLJ`, `scYU`), the PMF centroid force, and slab equilibration restraints — silently lands in group 0. In lipid systems this means `wca.setForceGroup(0)` (sim.py L277) makes group 0 a *mixture* of WCA repulsion plus all bonded/restraint terms, while groups 1–3 are pure nonbonded classes. In non-lipid systems, group 0 mixes AH with all bonded terms and group 1 is pure electrostatics. Keep this in mind whenever you interpret per-group energies.

Two additional force objects in `interactions.py` carry their own group conventions for lipid model variants not currently wired into `Sim`: the Cooke–Deserno cosine force sets group 2 (`interactions.py` L227) and the charge–nonpolar interaction sets group 1 (L251) — the latter's particle population is commented out in `add_interactions` (sim.py L530-L534). The `init_yu_interactions` function also contains a commented-out `yu.setForceGroup(1)` (L104), evidence that group assignment was deliberately moved out of the force factory and into `Sim`, where it can depend on system composition.

Sources: [sim.py](/calvados/sim.py#L269-L292), [sim.py](/calvados/sim.py#L317-L344), [interactions.py](/calvados/interactions.py#L217-L228), [interactions.py](/calvados/interactions.py#L241-L252), [interactions.py](/calvados/interactions.py#L92-L106)

## Interaction Groups: Pruning the Pair Space with TMT Classes

Before any force evaluates a pair, `CustomNonbondedForce.addInteractionGroup(setA, setB)` restricts evaluation to pairs drawn from the Cartesian product of two particle sets. `Sim.build_system` constructs these sets during the molecule loop by tracking **global particle indices** in Python sets keyed on the lipid `TMT` bead classification and net charge (sim.py L212-L263):

| Index set | Population rule | Code |
|---|---|---|
| `lipid_ser` | lipid beads with `tmt < 0` (negatively charged tails) | `lipid_indices & tmt_neg_indices` |
| `lipid_chd` | lipid beads with `-5 ≤ tmt < -4` (charged heads: CHO/PHO) | `lipid_indices & tmt_chd_indices` |
| `lipid_mid` | lipid beads with `tmt < -5` (midsection) | `lipid_indices & tmt_mid_indices` |
| `lipid_ltl` | lipid beads with `tmt > 0` (positive TMT tails) | `lipid_indices & tmt_pos_indices` |
| `charged_indices` | any bead with non-zero partial charge | `np.isclose(charge, 0.0)` check |

The interaction groups then encode the *physics topology* of each potential (sim.py L275-L289): WCA connects `lipid_ser ↔ (lipid_ltl | lipid_mid)` and `(proteins | ltl | chd | mid) ↔ (mid | chd)`; `ah_pp` is protein × protein only; the lipid AH force connects `lipid_ser ↔ (chd | ser | proteins)`; the SA attraction connects `(proteins | lipid_ltl) ↔ lipid_ltl`; and Yukawa connects `charged_indices ↔ charged_indices`. Because non-participating pairs are never evaluated, this pruning is also a performance optimization, not merely cosmetic — a system with one charged protein among thousands of neutral lipid beads pays electrostatics cost only on the charged subset.

Sources: [sim.py](/calvados/sim.py#L212-L219), [sim.py](/calvados/sim.py#L250-L263), [sim.py](/calvados/sim.py#L275-L289)

## The Exclusion Pipeline: From Local Bond Lists to Global Force Blacklists

Exclusions answer a different question than interaction groups: *which specific pairs should this force skip?* The pipeline is uniform across all component classes and follows one rule — **every pair whose interaction is represented by an explicit bonded term must be excluded from every nonbonded CustomNonbondedForce**. The flowchart below traces the complete path:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Sim.add_interactions(comp)<br/>per molecule, with global offset"] --> B["add_bonds → 1-2 bonded pairs"]
    A --> C["add_angles → angle-endpoint pairs"]
    A --> D["add_restraints → restrained pairs"]
    E["add_custom_restraints<br/>(file-specified pairs)"] --> F
    B --> F["Sim.add_exclusions(exclusion_map)"]
    C --> F
    D --> F
    F --> G{"nlipids > 0 ?"}
    G -->|Yes| H["addExclusion on wca, ah_pp, ah, sa, yu<br/>(5 forces × N pairs)"]
    G -->|No| I["addExclusion on ah, yu<br/>(2 forces × N pairs)"]
    H --> J["print_system_summary<br/>reports per-force exclusion counts"]
    I --> J
```

Each component class returns an `exclusion_map` — a list of `[global_i, global_j]` pairs — from its bond and angle population methods, and `Sim.add_exclusions` fans it out to every active nonbonded force in one loop (sim.py L487-L498). The exclusion policies per source differ by molecule class:

| Exclusion source | Component | Pair semantics | Policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Harmonic bonds | All classes (`add_bonds`) | Consecutive bonded beads (1-2) | Always excluded from AH/YU (and WCA/SA in lipid systems) |
| Angles | `Lipid.add_angles` | Beads i and i+2 (1-3) | Excluded |
| Angles | `RNA.add_angles` | Angle endpoints i and i+4 | Excluded (the intervening i+2 bead is already bond-excluded) |
| Harmonic/Go restraints | `Protein.add_restraints` via `Sim.add_restraints` | Every restrained pair | Excluded only if `exclude_nonbonded=True` (default) |
| Custom restraints | `Sim.add_custom_restraints` | File-specified pairs | Excluded if `exclude_nonbonded=True` |
| RNA base-base terms | `RNA.add_bonds` | Bases j = i+2 | Excluded from AH/YU, replaced by scaled bond term |

Two design details deserve emphasis. First, `Sim.add_restraints` accepts an `exclude_nonbonded` flag (sim.py L468-L473), so you can *add* a restraint on top of the native nonbonded interaction rather than replacing it — useful for probing how restraints perturb the baseline model. Second, restraint-driven exclusions are chemically significant: when a pair is restrained, its Ashbaugh-Hatch and Yukawa interaction is *removed* and (for the Go model) substituted, which is the subject of the next section.

Sources: [sim.py](/calvados/sim.py#L456-L498), [sim.py](/calvados/sim.py#L500-L544), [components.py](/calvados/components.py#L227-L238), [components.py](/calvados/components.py#L249-L281), [components.py](/calvados/components.py#L417-L430), [components.py](/calvados/components.py#L494-L524), [components.py](/calvados/components.py#L389-L415)

## Soft Exclusions: Scaled Bond Terms Replace Pair Interactions

A naive exclusion is binary — the pair either interacts or it does not. CALVADOS implements a **soft exclusion** pattern for cases where a graded residual interaction is physically desirable. Two subsystems use it:

**Go-model restrained pairs.** In `Protein.add_restraints`, any pair with Go scale ≥ `min_scale` (0.05) is added to the exclusion map, *removing* its native AH/YU interaction. But pairs below `cutoff_mix_in_LJYU` (0.15) simultaneously receive `CustomBondForce` replacements — `init_scaled_LJ` and `init_scaled_YU` (interactions.py L137-L158) — whose energy is multiplied by the per-pair `bondscale` factor derived from bfac/PAE confidence maps (components.py L155). The pair's interaction strength therefore interpolates continuously between "fully restrained + no nonbonded" and "weakly restrained + proportionally scaled nonbonded", avoiding the discontinuity a hard exclusion would impose on low-confidence contacts.

**RNA base-base stacking.** `RNA.init_bond_force` creates a dedicated `scLJ_rna` scaled-LJ force (components.py L336), and base pairs passing `basebase_check` (j = i+2, odd i) are added as scaled bonds with scale `n = rna_nb_scale` while their AH/YU counterparts are excluded (components.py L404-L414). The pattern is identical: blacklisted from the group-based force, reinstated as a pair-specific, parameterized bond.

> [!TIP]
> A pair in the exclusion map is not necessarily interaction-free. Always check whether the same pair appears in `scLJ`, `scYU`, or `scLJ_rna` before assuming zero nonbonded energy — the scaled bond forces are `CustomBondForce` objects and are unaffected by nonbonded exclusions.

Because these scaled forces are per-pair bonds, they inherit group 0 by default (see the force group map above). This means in a Go-restraint simulation, group 0's energy trace includes the scaled LJ/YU compensation terms — an important consideration when attributing energy changes to the restraint itself (see [AF-Guided Harmonic And Go Restraints](13-af-guided-harmonic-and-go-restraints) for the restraint physics and [Custom Restraints And PMF Forces](14-custom-restraints-and-pmf-forces) for the PMF centroid force, which also defaults to group 0).

Sources: [components.py](/calvados/components.py#L240-L281), [components.py](/calvados/components.py#L332-L343), [components.py](/calvados/components.py#L404-L414), [interactions.py](/calvados/interactions.py#L137-L158), [interactions.py](/calvados/interactions.py#L189-L204), [sim.py](/calvados/sim.py#L294-L304)

## Runtime Energy Decomposition with ForceGroupReporter

Force groups exist to be read. `ForceGroupReporter` (forcegroupreporter.py) is a compact OpenMM reporter that emits the potential energy of a single force group at every report interval, enabling you to watch, e.g., electrostatic energy drift or lipid SA relaxation independently of the total. Its mechanics hinge on OpenMM's bitmask convention: `Context.getState(..., groups=...)` accepts an integer whose bit *n* selects force group *n*, so selecting one group is `1 << group`:

```python
e = simulation.context.getState(getEnergy=True, groups=1 << self._group).getPotentialEnergy()
```

| API element | Signature / behavior | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Constructor | `ForceGroupReporter(file, reportInterval, group, append=False)` | `file` may be a path (opened/closed internally) or an open file object |
| Output format | Tab-separated `step<TAB>energy` header + rows | Energy in kJ/mol |
| `describeNextReport` | Returns `{'steps': ..., 'periodic': None, 'include': []}` | No positions/velocities requested — minimal state construction cost |
| `report` | Queries energy of group `self._group` only | Flushes every write for live monitoring |

The reporter is wired into the simulation module via `from .forcegroupreporter import ForceGroupReporter` in `sim.py` (L22), alongside `PressureDataReporter`. Because `groups` is a bitmask, you can also query multiple groups at once by OR-ing masks (`groups=(1<<1)|(1<<3)`) — useful when interpreting the merged group 1 in lipid systems, where protein-protein AH and lipid AH are intentionally reported together.

> [!TIP]
> The `include: []` return from `describeNextReport` is what makes this reporter cheap: OpenMM skips position/velocity/force computation for the report unless you request it. If you extend the reporter to also pull `groups`-filtered state objects, keep `periodic: None` so box vectors aren't forced into the state build.

Sources: [forcegroupreporter.py](/calvados/forcegroupreporter.py#L1-L25), [sim.py](/calvados/sim.py#L19-L23)

## Verification and Practical Guidance

`Sim.print_system_summary` (sim.py L374-L398) serializes the full system to XML and prints particle/exclusion counts per nonbonded force — your first stop when debugging exclusion mistakes. A mismatch between expected and reported exclusion counts almost always traces to one of three causes: (1) a `bond_check` returning `True` where the topology doesn't warrant a bond (note `Cyclic` adds the closing bond i=0 ↔ j=nbeads-1, components.py L564-L570, so cyclic peptides exclude that pair too); (2) restraint pairs added with `exclude_nonbonded=False` and thus absent from the summary; or (3) offsets — exclusion maps use *global* indices via `offset = self.nparticles - comp.nbeads` (sim.py L505), so any refactor that changes particle insertion order changes exclusions globally. When designing a new component class, the contract is simple: override `bond_check`/`angle_check`/`basebase_check` as static predicates, populate forces through `add_bonds`/`add_angles`, and return an exclusion map — `Sim` handles the fan-out. To observe the resulting energy decomposition at runtime, pair a `ForceGroupReporter` per group of interest with the workflow in [Sim Class Workflow](16-sim-class-workflow); the reporters themselves are covered further in [OpenMM Integration And Reporters](17-openmm-integration-and-reporters).

Sources: [sim.py](/calvados/sim.py#L374-L398), [sim.py](/calvados/sim.py#L505-L537), [components.py](/calvados/components.py#L558-L580)

## Where to Go Next

This page closes the "Force Field And Potentials" section. To continue the natural progression: study how the exclusion-linked restraints are constructed from structural data in [AF-Guided Harmonic And Go Restraints](13-af-guided-harmonic-and-go-restraints), how file-driven and PMF-based forces extend the same patterns in [Custom Restraints And PMF Forces](14-custom-restraints-and-pmf-forforces) and [Custom Restraints And PMF Forces](14-custom-restraints-and-pmf-forces), and how the assembled system finally runs in [Sim Class Workflow](16-sim-class-workflow). If you need the underlying potentials rather than their bookkeeping, return to [Ashbaugh-Hatch And Yukawa Potentials](10-ashbaugh-hatch-and-yukawa-potentials) and [Lipid Interactions: WCA And SA Terms](11-lipid-interactions-wca-and-sa-terms).

# AF-Guided Harmonic And Go Restraints



This page explains how MEM-CALVADOS enforces **folded structure** on coarse-grained protein beads using two AF-guided (AlphaFold-guided) restraint engines: **domain-bounded harmonic restraints** and **confidence-gated Go-type contacts**. Both engines share a single pipeline: geometry and confidence data are extracted from an AlphaFold PDB + PAE pair, contact pairs are selected per restraint type, and restraint forces are registered as OpenMM bond forces alongside the standard CALVADOS potentials. The page covers the force definitions in `interactions.py`, the selection/gating logic in the `Protein` class, the supporting parsers in `build.py`, default parameters, and how `Sim` wires everything at runtime.

## Architectural Layout: From AF Data To OpenMM Forces

The restraint subsystem is deliberately layered so that no OpenMM object is created before contact selection is complete. `build.py` owns **data extraction** (coordinates, pLDDT B-factors, PAE matrices, domain maps), `components.py` owns **selection and gating logic** inside the `Protein` class, and `interactions.py` owns **force-object construction**. `Sim.make_components` is the only orchestrator that decides *which* force flavor gets instantiated, passing the electrolyte-dependent Yukawa parameters (`eps_yu`, `k_yu`) that only Go restraints need.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Build["build.py (data extraction)"] {
        +geometry_from_pdb(pdb, use_com)
        +bfac_from_pdb(pdb, confidence)
        +load_pae(json, colabfold, symmetrize)
        +get_ssdomains(name, fdomains)
        +check_ssdomain(ssdomains, i, j)
    }
    class Protein["components.py :: Protein"] {
        +calc_x_from_pdb()
        +calc_dmap()
        +calc_ssdomains()
        +calc_go_scale()
        +calc_bondlength(i, j)
        +init_restraint_force(...)
        +add_restraints(offset, ...)
        +get_forces()
    }
    class Interactions["interactions.py (force layer)"] {
        +init_restraints(type)
        +add_single_restraint(cs, ...)
        +init_scaled_LJ(...)
        +init_scaled_YU(...)
    }
    class Sim["sim.py :: Sim"] {
        +make_components()
    }
    Build --> Protein : AF coordinates, PAE, pLDDT, domains
    Protein --> Interactions : bond/parameter registration
    Sim --> Protein : init_restraint_force with eps_yu, k_yu
```

The triggering condition is a single boolean: a component with `restraint = True` skips the generic spiral/linear initial geometry and instead reads its coordinates directly from `{pdb_folder}/{name}.pdb`, then branches on `restraint_type` to compute either the domain map (`calc_ssdomains`) or the Go contact scale (`calc_go_scale`).
Sources: [components.py](calvados/components.py#L177-L197), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L55-L106)

## The Force Layer: One Interface, Two Potential Forms

`interactions.init_restraints(restraint_type)` returns a polymorphic force object keyed on a single string. For `'harmonic'` it returns a plain `openmm.HarmonicBondForce`; for `'go'` it returns a `CustomBondForce` with the asymmetric Go energy expression `k*(5*(s/r)^12 - 6*(s/r)^10)` and two per-bond parameters, `s` (the equilibrium/natural contact distance) and `k` (the energy scale). This 12-10 form is minimized exactly at `r = s`, so unlike a 12-6 Lennard-Jones term it has no attractive tail below `s` — a contact compressed beyond its native distance is purely repulsive, which is the defining property of a Go model.

`add_single_restraint` is the single funnel through which every restraint bond passes. Note the unit asymmetry that follows from the two force types: harmonic `k` is supplied in `kJ/mol/nm²` (a second derivative of energy), while Go `k` is a plain `kJ/mol` energy scale packed with `s` into a per-bond parameter list. Every added pair is also returned as a 1-based record (`[i+1, j+1, dij, k]`) for later file output.

| Property | Harmonic engine | Go engine |
|---|---|---|
| OpenMM force class | `HarmonicBondForce` | `CustomBondForce` |
| Energy form | `k(dij)·(r − dij)²` | `k·(5(s/r)^12 − 6(s/r)^10)` |
| Per-bond parameters | `dij [nm]`, `k [kJ/mol/nm²]` | `s [nm]`, `k [kJ/mol]` |
| Selection criterion | Both residues in a structured domain, `dij ≤ cutoff_restr` | `scale[i,j] ≥ min_scale` (confidence gate) |
| Extra companion forces | none | `scLJ`, `scYU` pseudo-bond forces |
Sources: [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L124-L135), [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L172-L187)

## AF Model Ingestion: Coordinates, pLDDT, and PAE

Three parsers in `build.py` convert AlphaFold artifacts into restraint inputs. `geometry_from_pdb` extracts either CA positions (`name CA` selection) or per-residue centers of mass when `use_com=True`, dividing by 10 to convert Å → nm, and returns the PDB's unit-cell dimensions as the local frame. The `use_com` choice matters because CALVADOS beads represent whole residues: COM placement keeps the restraint network centered on the residue body rather than the backbone trace.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["AF PDB file"] --> B["geometry_from_pdb<br/>CA or COM → xinit [nm]"]
    A --> C["bfac_from_pdb<br/>mean tempfactors / 100 → pLDDT map"]
    D["AF JSON (PAE)"] --> E["load_pae<br/>symmetrize, Å → nm (/10)"]
    B --> F["dmap<br/>(self_distances)"]
    C --> G["bfac_map = min.outer(bfac, bfac)"]
    E --> H["scale = bfac_sigm × pae_sigm"]
    G --> H
    F --> H2["harmonic selection + Go s distances"]
    H --> I["Go contact gating"]
```

`bfac_from_pdb` reads AlphaFold's per-residue confidence (pLDDT), which AF stores in the B-factor column, averaging atom tempfactors per residue and scaling to [0, 1]; the `confidence` argument acts as a hard floor (the `Protein` caller passes `confidence=0.`, deferring all filtering to the smooth sigmoid instead of a binary cut). `load_pae` handles the three PAE JSON dialects in circulation — EBI AlphaFold (`colabfold=0`, a list of dicts with key `predicted_aligned_error`), ColabFold legacy (`colabfold=1`, top-level dict with `predicted_aligned_error`), and newer ColabFold (`colabfold=2`, key `pae`) — and symmetrizes the matrix as `0.5·(PAE + PAEᵀ)` before conversion to nm.
Sources: [build.py](calvados/build.py#L290-L321), [build.py](calvados/build.py#L331-L343), [components.py](calvados/components.py#L124-L128), [components.py](calvados/components.py#L66-L70)

> [!TIP]
> The PAE matrix in AF JSON files is in **Ångströms** — `calc_go_scale` divides by 10 immediately after loading (`/ 10. # in nm`). If you supply a PAE file in a nonstandard format, an uncaught 10× unit error silently shifts every sigmoid gate, effectively enabling or disabling the entire Go network.

## Engine 1: AF-Guided Harmonic Restraints (Domain-Bounded)

The harmonic engine restains pairs *within annotated folded domains* rather than relying on per-pair confidence scores. `calc_ssdomains` reads `fdomains` (default `domains.yaml`) — a YAML mapping protein name → list of domains, where a domain may be a flat `[start, end]` range or a list of sub-ranges — and expands each 1-based inclusive range into a 0-based residue set. A dPAM CSV format (`uniprot`/`range` columns) is also supported via the `dpam` flag.

Selection happens in `Protein.add_restraints`, which sweeps the strict upper triangle (`j ≥ i+2`, excluding chain neighbors) with three filters applied in order:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S["pair (i, j), j ≥ i+2"] --> Q1{"dmap[i,j] ≤ cutoff_restr<br/>(default 0.9 nm)?"}
    Q1 -- no --> X["skip"]
    Q1 -- yes --> Q2{"restraint_type?"}
    Q2 -- harmonic --> Q3{"check_ssdomain<br/>req_both=True:<br/>i AND j in same domain?"}
    Q3 -- no --> X
    Q3 -- yes --> K1["k = k_harmonic (700)"] --> R["add_single_restraint<br/>d = dmap[i,j]"]
    Q2 -- go --> Q4{"scale[i,j] ≥ min_scale<br/>(0.05)?"}
    Q4 -- no --> X
    Q4 -- yes --> K2["k = k_go × scale[i,j]"] --> MIX{"scale < cutoff_mix_in_LJYU (0.15)?"}
    MIX -- yes --> SC["add scaled pseudo-LJ/YU pair<br/>(scYU only if q_i·q_j ≠ 0)"]
    MIX -- no --> R2["add_single_restraint"]
    SC --> R2
    R --> E["record exclusion_map pair"]
    R2 --> E
```

Critically, the harmonic engine also rewrites the **covalent chain** inside annotated domains: `calc_bondlength` is called by `add_bonds` for every consecutive pair, and when *either* residue belongs to a structured domain (`req_both=False`), the generic residue bond length `d0` is replaced by the true PDB distance `dmap[i,j]`. This pre-loads the backbone geometry of folded regions so that harmonic restraints stabilize an already-correct local fold rather than pulling a spiral into one.
Sources: [build.py](calvados/build.py#L345-L389), [components.py](calvados/components.py#L249-L281), [components.py](calvados/components.py#L199-L218), [components.py](calvados/components.py#L94-L105)

## Engine 2: Confidence-Gated Go Contacts

The Go engine replaces the binary domain map with a **continuous, per-pair confidence gate** computed from two independent AF signals multiplied together in `calc_go_scale`:

1. **pLDDT gate** — the outer-minimum of residue confidences (`np.minimum.outer(bfac, bfac)`) ensures a contact is only as trusted as its *weakest* participant, squashed through a logistic sigmoid `σ(bfac_width·(bfac_map − bfac_shift))` with defaults `bfac_width=50.`, `bfac_shift=0.8`.
2. **PAE gate** — the symmetrized PAE value itself (in nm) enters with inverted sign, `σ(−pae_width·(pae − pae_shift))`, so low alignment error (high confidence) saturates the gate; defaults `pae_width=15.`, `pae_shift=0.3`.

Their product is `self.scale ∈ (0, 1)`, which plays three distinct roles:

| Role | Mechanism | Threshold logic |
|---|---|---|
| Contact admission | `k = k_go × scale[i,j]` | skip if `scale < 0.05` (`min_scale`) |
| Interaction-regime switch | choose pure Go vs. mixed regime | boundary at `cutoff_mix_in_LJYU = 0.15` |
| Backbone blending | `bondscale = σ(−80·(scale − 0.1))` blends chain bond length between generic `d0` and PDB distance | continuous, per pair |

The mixed regime (`0.05 ≤ scale < 0.15`) is the most subtle part of the design. Weakly confident native contacts still receive a Go bond, but simultaneously the **standard Ashbaugh-Hatch/Yukawa pair potential between those two beads is replaced** by `init_scaled_LJ` / `init_scaled_YU` pseudo-bonds whose per-bond scale factor is `bondscale[i,j]` — a second sigmoid that rises as `scale` falls. This prevents double-counting: without the substitution, a weak native contact would experience both the LJ/YU attraction *and* the Go well, and the Go bond would additionally suppress the excluded-volume that the regular nonbonded force provides. For charged pairs only (`q_i·q_j ≠ 0`), a matching scaled Yukawa bond is added. The substitution bonds carry the raw `eps_lj`, `cutoff_lj`, `eps_yu`, `k_yu` values injected from `Sim` into `init_restraint_force`.
Sources: [components.py](calvados/components.py#L136-L155), [components.py](calvados/components.py#L240-L281), [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L137-L158), [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L189-L204)

> [!TIP]
> Read the two sigmoids as **complementary gates on the same quantity**: `scale` gates the Go force *open* as confidence rises, while `bondscale` gates the *residual* LJ/YU interaction open as confidence falls. At `scale ≈ 0.1` both are mid-transition — this is why the backbone blending uses the same crossover region. When debugging a system where a domain "falls apart" or "clumps", inspect `scaled_LJ_{name}.txt` and `restr_{name}.txt` outputs: their pair lists should partition the contact set below and above `cutoff_mix_in_LJYU`.

## Runtime Wiring In `Sim` And Artifact Output

`Sim.make_components` instantiates each component class by `molecule_type`, and for any component whose effective properties carry `restraint=True` it calls `init_restraint_force` — **with** the system-level LJ/YU parameters when `restraint_type == 'go'` (the scaled pseudo-bond forces need them at construction time), and bare otherwise — then flips the system-wide flag `use_restraints`, which downstream code uses to decide whether restraint forces join the system. Note that `eps_yu` and `k_yu` are computed by `genParamsDH(temp, ionic)` inside `build_system` *before* `make_components` runs, which is the dependency ordering that makes the Go pathway possible.

Every restraint is persisted for inspection: `write_restraints` emits `restr_{name}.txt` (pair, distance, force constant), plus `scaled_LJ_{name}.txt` and `scaled_YU_{name}.txt` for Go systems, and `get_forces` appends `cs` (and `scLJ`, `scYU` for Go) to the component's force list that `Sim` later registers.
Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L94-L104), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L152-L156), [components.py](calvados/components.py#L283-L307)

## Default Parameter Reference

All restraint knobs live in the component defaults (`calvados/data/default_component.yaml`) and can be overridden globally via `Components(**defaults)` or per-molecule via `components.add(name=..., restraint=True, ...)` — the `cfg.Components` class merges package defaults with user kwargs into the `defaults` block that every component falls back on.

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `restraint` | `false` | Master switch; routes geometry to PDB instead of spiral/linear build |
| `restraint_type` | `'harmonic'` | `'harmonic'` or `'go'` |
| `cutoff_restr` | `0.9` nm | Max native distance for a restraint pair (both engines) |
| `k_harmonic` | `700.` | Harmonic force constant, `kJ/mol/nm²` |
| `fdomains` | `'domains.yaml'` | Domain map file (YAML name→ranges, or dPAM CSV) |
| `k_go` | `15.` | Go energy scale (max), `kJ/mol`, scaled by `scale[i,j]` |
| `use_com` | `true` | Bead positions from residue COM instead of CA |
| `colabfold` | `0` | PAE JSON dialect: 0=EBI AF, 1=ColabFold, 2=ColabFold (`pae` key) |
| `bfac_shift` / `bfac_width` | `0.8` / `50.` | pLDDT sigmoid midpoint / steepness |
| `pae_shift` / `pae_width` | `0.3` / `15.` | PAE sigmoid midpoint (nm) / steepness |
| `min_scale` / `cutoff_mix_in_LJYU` | `0.05` / `0.15` (call-site) | Go admission floor / mixed-regime boundary |
| `bscale_shift` / `bscale_width` | `0.1` / `80` (call-site) | `bondscale` sigmoid parameters |
Sources: [default_component.yaml](calvados/data/default_component.yaml#L13-L30), [cfg.py](calvados/cfg.py#L64-L95)

## Worked Configurations From The Examples

The `single_GO` example demonstrates the full Go pathway on a multi-domain protein (hnRNPA1S or TIA1): the component is created with `restraint=True`, `restraint_type='go'`, `use_com=True`, `colabfold=0`, and `k_go=10.`, with `pdb_folder` pointing at a directory holding the AF PDB and its PAE JSON (e.g. `AF-P00698.json`). The `single_TMP_AF` example shows the **per-component override pattern**: defaults set the Go parameters (`k_go=15.`) once for all components, but `restraint=True` is applied only to the transmembrane protein via `components.add(name=args.name, restraint=True, ...)`, leaving the POPC lipid component — which has no PDB/PAE — fully unrestrained. This is the canonical way to mix folded-protein restraints with free (lipid, RNA, crowder) components in one system.

| Example | Engine activated | Key settings |
|---|---|---|
| `single_GO` | Go, whole component | `restraint=True`, `restraint_type='go'`, `k_go=10.`, AF PDB+JSON in `input/` |
| `single_TMP_AF` | Go, protein only | defaults `k_go=15.`, per-component `add(..., restraint=True)` beside lipid component |
Sources: [prepare.py](examples/single_GO/prepare.py#L49-L68), [README.md](examples/single_GO/README.md#L1-L9), [prepare.py](examples/single_TMP_AF/prepare.py#L71-L92)

## Engine Selection Guidance

The two engines embody different philosophies and the choice is structural, not stylistic. Choose **harmonic** when you have trusted domain annotations (`domains.yaml`) and want maximal rigidity — a single uniform force constant, backbone distances pre-loaded inside domains, zero configuration beyond the domain file. Choose **Go** when domain annotations are unavailable or unreliable: the AF confidence signals (`bfac`, PAE) act as a *self-annotating* domain map, graded force constants let marginal contacts break, and the LJ/YU substitution keeps weak-contact regions physically consistent with the CALVADOS force field rather than over-stabilized.

| Dimension | Harmonic | Go |
|---|---|---|
| Required inputs | PDB + `fdomains` YAML | PDB + PAE JSON only |
| Confidence usage | implicit (via domain curation) | explicit, per-pair, continuous |
| Force constant | uniform (`k_harmonic`) | graded (`k_go × scale`) |
| Backbone geometry | rewritten inside domains only | continuously blended by `bondscale` |
| Risk profile | over-rigid if domain map is wrong | over-soft if AF confidence is systematically low |

For the adjacent restraint machinery — external forces and PMF-based tabulated potentials — continue to [Custom Restraints And PMF Forces](14-custom-restraints-and-pmf-forces); for how these forces are registered into force groups and excluded from nonbonded pair lists, see [Force Groups And Interaction Exclusions](12-force-groups-and-interaction-exclusions); for the equilibration restraints that hold slab systems together before production, see [Slab Equilibration And Barostats](15-slab-equilibration-and-barostats).

# Custom Restraints And PMF Forces



CALVADOS ships two extension mechanisms that operate *outside* the standard AF-guided restraint pipeline: **custom restraints** (arbitrary user-defined restraint pairs supplied via a text file) and the **PMF force** (a tabulated potential of mean force between protein and bilayer centroids). Both are optional Config flags that hook into `Sim.build_system` and are materialized as OpenMM bond-based forces. This page documents the data flow, input formats, force initialization, exclusion strategy, and verification path for both mechanisms, at the level of detail needed to extend or debug them.

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L294-L304), [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L113-L135)

## Architecture Overview

Both mechanisms follow the same lifecycle: a declarative user input is parsed during system construction, converted to absolute particle indices, instantiated as an OpenMM force object, and finally attached to the `openmm.System` after all per-component interactions are in place.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Custom Restraints
        A["cres.txt<br/>name copy bead | name copy bead | r k"] -->|"parse_custom_restraints"| B["[i, j, r, k] with symbolic names"]
        B -->|"map_custom_restraints"| C["custom_restr_abs<br/>absolute 0-based bead indices"]
        C -->|"add_custom_restraints"| D["cres force<br/>HarmonicBondForce or CustomBondForce"]
        D --> E["AH/YU exclusions<br/>for restrained pairs"]
    end
    subgraph PMF Force
        F["fpmf (.npy)<br/>tabulated u(dz)"] -->|"np.load"| G["Continuous1DFunction<br/>over [-Lz/2, Lz/2]"]
        G --> H["CustomCentroidBondForce<br/>protein group ↔ lipid group"]
    end
    E --> I["system.addForce"]
    H --> I
```

The critical ordering constraint: custom restraints and the PMF force are wired **after** the component loop completes (they need full particle-index space and the `protein_indices` / `lipid_indices` sets), whereas component-internal restraints are added per molecule inside the loop.

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L294-L304), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L317-L373)

## Custom Restraints: Input Format And Symbolic Mapping

The custom restraint file (configured via `fcustom_restraints`) uses a pipe-delimited, one-restraint-per-line format:

```
hnRNPA1S 1 72 | hnRNPA1S 1 157 | 0.559 700.0
```

Each line encodes five values: component `name`, `copy` number, `bead` number for both partners (1-based, per the in-code comment), the target distance `r` in nm, and the force constant `k`.

| Field | Position | Convention | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | token 1 / token 5 | string | Component name in `components.yaml` |
| `copy` | token 2 / token 6 | 1-based | Copy index for multi-molecule components (`nmol > 1`) |
| `bead` | token 3 / token 7 | 1-based | Bead/residue index within the molecule |
| `r` | token 9 | nm | Equilibrium restraint distance |
| `k` | token 10 | kJ/mol/nm² (harmonic) or kJ/mol (Go) | Force constant |

Sources: [cres.txt](examples/custom_restraints/input/cres.txt#L1-L8), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L604-L616)

`Sim.parse_custom_restraints` is a static method that reads the file and yields 4-element records `[i, j, r, k]`, where `i` and `j` are the `[name, copy, bead]` triples. `Sim.map_custom_restraints` then resolves symbolic names to **absolute, 0-based particle indices** in the global system. It first accumulates a bead offset per component — `total_beads` grows by `comp.nmol * comp.nbeads` per component, and `comp.start_bead` records the running base — then computes:

```python
x_abs = comp.start_bead + (copy-1)*comp.nbeads + (bead-1)
```

This design decouples the restraint file from system layout: restraints survive reordering of components and multi-copy expansion without the user ever touching OpenMM indices.

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L596-L616), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L618-L620)

## Force Initialization And The Exclusion Strategy

`Sim.add_custom_restraints` instantiates the force via `interactions.init_restraints(self.custom_restraint_type)` and dispatches parameterization through the shared `add_single_restraint` helper. The force type is selected by the `custom_restraint_type` config key:

| Type | OpenMM Force | Energy Form | Per-bond Parameters | Units of `k` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `harmonic` | `HarmonicBondForce` | ½k(r−r₀)² | `r₀` (nm), `k` | kJ/mol/nm² |
| `go` | `CustomBondForce` | `k*(5*(s/r)^12-6*(s/r)^10)` | `s` (nm), `k` (kJ/mol) | kJ/mol |

Both variants enable periodic boundary conditions via `setUsesPeriodicBoundaryConditions(True)`.

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L475-L485), [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L124-L135), [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L172-L187)

Every restrained pair is also registered in an `exclusion_map` and passed to `Sim.add_exclusions`, which removes the pair from the native nonbonded forces — `ah` and `yu` in protein-only systems, plus `wca`, `ah_pp`, and `sa` in lipid systems. This is the double-counting safeguard: a custom restraint *replaces* the default Lennard-Jones/Debye-Hückel contact rather than augmenting it. If you pass `exclude_nonbonded=False`, restraint pairs keep their native interactions on top of the restraint potential — rarely the physical intent.

> [!TIP]
> Force ordering in the serialized system is deterministic but positional: for a single-protein system the force stack is `[ah, yu, hb, cres]`, which is why the test retrieves `system.getForces()[3]` for the custom restraint force. Enabling component-level restraints (which append `cs` per component) or extra forces shifts this index — deserialize and search by force type rather than hardcoding indices in downstream tooling.

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L484-L498), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L346-L349), [test_custom_restraints.py](tests/test_custom_restraints.py#L99-L107)

## PMF Force: Tabulated Protein–Bilayer Potential

The PMF mechanism computes an effective interaction between two **centroids** — the collection of all protein beads and the collection of all lipid beads — along the periodic box z-axis. The construction in `interactions.init_pmf_force` combines two OpenMM primitives:

1. **`Continuous1DFunction`** — the array `u` loaded from `fpmf` (a `.npy` file via `np.load`) is interpolated into a smooth tabulated function spanning `[-Lz/2, Lz/2]` with periodic continuation enabled.
2. **`CustomCentroidBondForce(2, ...)`** — computes `dz = z1 - z2 - Lz*floor((z1-z2)/Lz + 0.5)`, the minimum-image z-separation between group centroids, and evaluates `pmf(dz)`.

```python
table = openmm.Continuous1DFunction(list(map(float, u)), -Lz/2., Lz/2., True)
f = openmm.CustomCentroidBondForce(2, f'pmf(dz); dz=z1-z2-{Lz}*floor((z1-z2)/{Lz}+0.5)')
f.addTabulatedFunction('pmf', table)
f.setUsesPeriodicBoundaryConditions(True)
```

The floor-based minimum-image expression is what makes the potential periodic: a protein crossing the box boundary in z continues to sample the same PMF curve. Because `Lz` is interpolated directly into the expression string, changing the box size invalidates the domain of the tabulated function — regenerate the table (and the `.npy` file) whenever `box[2]` changes.

Sources: [interactions.py](calvados/interactions.py#L113-L118)

Wiring happens in `Sim.build_system` after the molecule loop, gated on the `pmf_force` config flag. The two centroid groups are built from the `protein_indices` and `lipid_indices` sets accumulated during particle enumeration (sorted for deterministic ordering), then connected by a single centroid bond:

```python
u = np.load(self.fpmf)
self.pmf = interactions.init_pmf_force(u, self.box[2])
g_pep = self.pmf.addGroup(sorted(protein_indices))
g_lip = self.pmf.addGroup(sorted(lipid_indices))
self.pmf.addBond([g_pep, g_lip], [])
```

The force is added to the system last, after the barostat conditional block, in `add_forces_to_system`. Note this is a *collective* coordinate by design — one PMF between two ensembles, not per-molecule forces — so it requires a system containing both proteins and lipids (the `protein_indices` / `lipid_indices` sets are only populated for those molecule types).

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L298-L304), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L371-L372), [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L244-L248)

## Configuration Reference

Both mechanisms are activated purely through `Config` keyword arguments (each key is applied as a `Sim` attribute via the generic config setattr loop) plus, for PMF, a data file path:

| Config Key | Type | Effect | Consumed By |
|---|---|---|---|
| `custom_restraints` | `bool` | Triggers parsing, mapping, force creation, exclusions, and `system.addForce` | `build_system` |
| `custom_restraint_type` | `str` | `'harmonic'` or `'go'` — selects `HarmonicBondForce` vs. Go-style `CustomBondForce` | `init_restraints` |
| `fcustom_restraints` | `str` | Path to the pipe-delimited restraint file | `parse_custom_restraints` |
| `pmf_force` | `bool` | Triggers PMF force construction and centroid-group wiring | `build_system` |
| `fpmf` | `str` | Path to `.npy` array with PMF values | `np.load` in `build_system` |

A minimal activation in a `prepare.py`-style script:

```python
config = Config(
    ...
    custom_restraints = True,
    custom_restraint_type = 'harmonic',
    fcustom_restraints = f'{cwd}/input/cres.txt',
)
```

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L31-L33), [prepare.py](examples/custom_restraints/prepare.py#L45-L47), [test_custom_restraints.py](tests/test_custom_restraints.py#L73-L76)

## Verification: The Test Harness Pattern

`tests/test_custom_restraints.py` establishes the canonical verification pattern: build a minimal single-protein system with custom restraints enabled, run `sim.run`, then round-trip the system through OpenMM XML serialization and introspect the force stack:

```python
system = openmm.XmlSerializer.deserialize(open(f"{cwd}/tests/data/{sysname}/{sysname}.xml").read())
force = system.getForces()[3]
N = force.getNumBonds()
f = force.getBondParameters(0)
i, j = f[0], f[1]
assert (N == 1) and (i == 0) and (j == 9)
```

The assertion validates the full symbolic-to-absolute mapping chain end-to-end: the restraint declared against named beads must materialize as exactly one bond between absolute indices 0 and 9 in the serialized system. This is also a regression guard on `map_custom_restraints` offset arithmetic — any change to component ordering or bead accounting that breaks `start_bead` accumulation will fail here.

Sources: [test_custom_restraints.py](tests/test_custom_restraints.py#L54-L107)

## Worked Example: `examples/custom_restraints`

The example combines both restraint layers on a single hnRNPA1S construct. The end-to-end flow from user input to serialized system:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["prepare.py<br/>Config + Components"] --> B["config.yaml<br/>custom_restraints=True"]
    A --> C["components.yaml<br/>fdomains, restraint_type"]
    B --> D["sim.run"]
    C --> D
    D --> E["AF-guided harmonic<br/>restraints (ssdomains)"]
    D --> F["cres.txt mapping<br/>8 custom restraints"]
    E --> G["top.pdb + system.xml"]
    F --> G
```

In the example's `Config`, `custom_restraints = True` with `custom_restraint_type = 'harmonic'` and `fcustom_restraints` pointing at `input/cres.txt`, whose 8 lines each restrain a bead in the N-terminal folded domain to a bead in the C-terminal domain at distances of ~0.5–1.1 nm with `k = 700.0`. The same script separately configures `Components` with `fdomains`/`restraint_type`/`k_harmonic` — that is the AF-guided pipeline (sequence extraction from PDB, substructure-domain distance maps, AH/YU exclusions) and is covered in [AF-Guided Harmonic And Go Restraints](13-af-guided-harmonic-and-go-restraints). The important architectural point is that the two layers coexist multiplicatively in one system: component restraints attach per-molecule inside the build loop, custom restraints attach once globally afterward, each maintaining its own exclusion bookkeeping.

Sources: [prepare.py](examples/custom_restraints/prepare.py#L26-L48), [prepare.py](examples/custom_restraints/prepare.py#L64-L82), [cres.txt](examples/custom_restraints/input/cres.txt#L1-L8), [domains.yaml](examples/custom_restraints/input/domains.yaml#L1-L3)

> [!TIP]
> When authoring `cres.txt` for multi-copy components, remember `copy` and `bead` are 1-based while the resolved indices are 0-based absolute particle numbers; the verbose run output prints every mapped `(name, copy, bead, r, k)` tuple during `map_custom_restraints` — cross-check those prints against `start_bead` accumulation before launching long productions.

Sources: [sim.py](calvados/sim.py#L604-L616)
